properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Written notice required to owner before reporting if value exceeds $50

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Includes payroll, vendor, and dividend checks

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Electronic indicators of owner interest such as online account access may count as activity

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; distributions or required minimum distributions do not reset dormancy if owner-initiated contact has ceased
properties.notes: Special care required — early reporting can significantly impact owner retirement planning

properties.triggerDescription: Date policy matures or date of confirmed death of insured, whichever is applicable
properties.notes: Insurer must check Social Security Death Master File periodically

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or card issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Some exemptions may apply for cards with expiration dates issued prior to certain statutory changes

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Includes patient credit balances in healthcare settings. Government payor overpayments subject to separate federal rules.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: First-class mail notice required at least 90 days before filing. Certified mail required for property valued at $1,000 or more at least 60 days before filing. Banks must also publish newspaper notice for property over $50.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Includes payroll, wages, salary, and vendor checks

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Certified mail required for accounts over $1,000. Annual certified mailing required for dividend reinvestment plan accounts.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; age-based triggers may apply based on owner date of birth
properties.notes: Escheatment of IRA triggers a taxable distribution — holder must withhold 10% federal income tax and issue Form 1099-R. Securities must be liquidated before transfer.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date. New regulation requires holders to confirm death within 90 days of receiving notice.
properties.notes: If death confirmation attempts fail, last date of owner-generated activity is used for dormancy. Joint accounts — valid activity by one owner may prevent dormancy trigger.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Gift cards may not expire earlier than 9 years after issuance or last load date. Inactivity fees and dormancy fees are prohibited under NY General Business Law § 396-i.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes accounts receivable and accounts payable credits. Healthcare patient credit balances subject to same rules.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: California requires a two-step reporting process: a Holder Notice Report followed by a Holder Remit Report. Properties under $50 typically receive no owner notification before escheat.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Payroll, wages, and commissions have a shorter 1-year dormancy period

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Holders must send notice to owners of securities regardless of value prior to reporting

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; age-based triggers may apply
properties.notes: California is one of the largest unclaimed property programs in the US ($15B+ held). IRA reporting requires careful attention to federal tax implications.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Life insurance companies follow a separate report cycle — Holder Notice Report due April 30, Holder Remit Report due December 1-15.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Unused gift certificates are generally excluded from California unclaimed property law and are not escheated to the state.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes customer overpayments and patient credit balances. California has some of the most aggressive enforcement in the nation.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Due diligence required for property valued at $250 or more. Notice must be sent by May 1. Annual reports due July 1.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Payroll checks have a 1-year dormancy period in Texas, shorter than most other property types

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Texas specifically requires reporting of unclaimed mineral proceeds and royalties, unusual among states

properties.triggerDescription: Generally 3 years after owner reaches required minimum distribution (RMD) age and stops interacting with account
properties.notes: Roth IRAs may not be reportable unless specific abandonment conditions are met. Rules may vary based on federal tax regulations.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Life insurance proceeds are now due with all other unclaimed funds on July 1 each year following HB 1514.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Negative reports required in Texas even if no property to report — one of few states with this requirement.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes customer overpayments and patient credit balances. Texas has a business-to-business exemption that may apply to certain commercial credit balances.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Annual reports due April 30. Florida uses a calendar year ending December 31 as the cut-off date.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Payroll checks have a 1-year dormancy period. Other checks follow the standard dormancy period for their property type.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Florida reduced securities dormancy to 3 years. Covers stock, equity interests, unmatured/unredeemed debt, and matured/redeemed debt.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; age-based triggers may apply based on required minimum distribution age
properties.notes: Florida follows the standard 5-year dormancy for IRAs. Federal RMD rules interact with state dormancy determinations.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Report must include insured's full name, TIN/SSN, date of birth, and last known address of insured and beneficiary.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Florida follows standard 5-year dormancy for gift certificates and store credit.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes patient credit balances and customer overpayments. Late reports subject to penalties under FL Stat. § 717.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Due diligence required since September 10, 2016 for property of $50 or more, sent 60-120 days before reporting. Annual reports due April 15.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Payroll and commission checks have a shorter 1-year dormancy period. Other outstanding checks generally follow the standard 3-year period.

properties.triggerDescription: Lost contact standard — property is not reportable if owner increases, decreases, or accepts principal within the 3-year period. Holder/transfer agent due diligence also governed by SEC regulations.
properties.notes: Pennsylvania's 'lost contact' standard is designed to prevent reporting of securities that are merely held in a passive investment account rather than truly abandoned.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; fiduciary-held property including IRAs follows the standard 3-year dormancy period
properties.notes: Pennsylvania Treasury issued Policy Guidance in 2016 specifically to ensure IRA and retirement account owners are not subject to negative tax treatment from escheatment.

properties.triggerDescription: Date proceeds become due and payable under the policy; a policy not matured by actual proof of death is deemed matured if the policy was in force when the insured reached limiting age
properties.notes: Life insurance reports also due April 15. Demutualization proceeds are treated as a distinct property type.

properties.triggerDescription: Two years after the redemption period expires, or 3 years from date of issuance if no redemption period was specified
properties.notes: 'Qualified gift certificates' (no expiration date, no fees) are generally exempt from escheatment reporting under Pennsylvania law.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes patient credit balances and customer overpayments. Pennsylvania has intensified audit enforcement, often extending back 15+ years.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Illinois Revised Uniform Unclaimed Property Act (IRUUPA) reduced most dormancy periods from 5 years to 3 years. Written notice required 60+ days before filing for property of $50 or more.

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Payroll checks have a 1-year dormancy period. Money orders have a 5-year period; traveler's checks have an unusually long 15-year period.

properties.triggerDescription: Earliest of 3 years after first RPO mailing, or 5 years after the owner's last indication of interest in the security
properties.notes: Illinois uses a hybrid RPO/inactivity standard that is less favorable to owners than RUUPA's federal-securities-law-aligned standard. If the owner's death is confirmed, the security is presumed abandoned 2 years after the date of death.

properties.triggerDescription: 3 years after the later of an RPO event or the date of mandatory distribution (age-based or death-triggered)
properties.notes: Updated from the prior standard (5 years after mandatory distribution age) to follow RUUPA's approach with Illinois-specific variations.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Life insurance reports due before May 1; banking/financial institution reports due before November 1.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Gift cards with no expiration date, no dormancy/inactivity/service fees, and no cash redemption value are generally exempt from reporting.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes patient credit balances and customer overpayments. Record retention requirement of 10 years after report creates an effective 13-year compliance window.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Due diligence notices typically sent 60-120 days before the reporting deadline. Annual report deadline is July 1.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Includes uncashed payroll and dividend checks. Standard 3-year dormancy applies; utility deposits are a shorter 1-year exception.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable (RPO), whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Includes stock and mutual fund shares with no owner contact for the dormancy period.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; treated as a distribution for tax purposes upon escheatment
properties.notes: Escheatment of an IRA requires the custodian to withhold 10% for federal income tax and issue Form 1099-R, since the transfer is treated as a distribution under the IRC.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Demutualization proceeds of insurance companies are treated as a distinct property type with their own presumption rules under MCL 567.228b.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Gift certificates, gift cards, and credit memos are governed by a dedicated provision (MCL 567.235) with specific presumption-of-abandonment rules.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Includes patient credit balances and customer overpayments. Michigan imposes no statute of limitations for owners to later reclaim escheated property.
properties.statute: MCL 567.221 et seq. (Uniform Unclaimed Property Act)

properties.triggerDescription: 3 years after maturity or 3 years after the date of last owner-indicated interest, whichever is earlier
properties.notes: Due diligence notices sent 60-180 days before the report date for property valued at $50 or more, by first-class mail or email. Items under $50 may be reported in the aggregate.

properties.triggerDescription: Date compensation or check became payable
properties.notes: Compensation for personal services (payroll) has a 1-year dormancy period under IC 32-34-1-25.

properties.triggerDescription: 3 years after the earlier of the date of the last unclaimed dividend/distribution or the date of a second mailing returned as undeliverable
properties.notes: Applies to stock, dividends, profits, distributions, interest, and other sums held by a business association for shareholders or other security holders.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity; aligns generally with Indiana's standard 3-year dormancy approach
properties.notes: Indiana allows a 25-year window for owners or heirs to claim escheated property — longer than the indefinite/no-limit approach in some neighboring states.

properties.triggerDescription: Amount due and payable under the terms of an insurance policy
properties.notes: Demutualization of insurance company property is treated as a distinct presumption category under IC 32-34-1-28.5.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of last owner-initiated transaction or date of issuance if no activity
properties.notes: Unused airline tickets are explicitly listed alongside gift cards as a covered property type under Indiana's definition of intangible property.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Indiana explicitly excludes business-to-business credit memoranda from the definition of reportable property, an exemption healthcare and corporate holders should review carefully.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated activity on the account
properties.notes: Due diligence notice required at least 60 days before filing for property of $100 or more. A 'notice of inactivity' is sent regardless of remittance status. Annual reports due November 1 (May 1 for life insurance).

properties.triggerDescription: Date check was issued
properties.notes: Accounts payable, payroll, and accounts receivable items typically follow the standard 3-year dormancy period.

properties.triggerDescription: Last owner-initiated contact or first instance of mail returned as undeliverable, whichever occurs first
properties.notes: Strong 'active relationship' carve-out — if the owner maintains an active relationship with the holder on ANY account, no property of that owner is remitted, even dormant trust or investment accounts.

properties.triggerDescription: 3 years after the earliest of: the date of distribution or attempted distribution, the date of required distribution under the plan, or the date specified under federal income tax law
properties.notes: Massachusetts has clean, explicit regulatory language for IRA/qualified plan dormancy triggers under 960 CMR 4.03(12) — among the most clearly codified of any state reviewed.

properties.triggerDescription: Date of confirmed death of insured or policy maturity date
properties.notes: Life insurance companies file on a separate May 1 deadline rather than the standard November 1 deadline.

properties.triggerDescription: Seven years from date of purchase
properties.notes: Massachusetts gift cards/certificates may not expire for at least 7 years from purchase, one of the longest minimum validity periods in the country, effective since June 2003.

properties.triggerDescription: Date credit balance was established or last owner-initiated activity
properties.notes: Massachusetts regulation explicitly states that commercial customers incorporated in Massachusetts are NOT exempt from credit balance reporting obligations in other states' jurisdictions — a notable cross-border compliance note for multi-state healthcare and corporate holders.
